title: Heavy-tier harness 1/5: nested environment — childEnv(mode) beside isolate-run.js
description:
Piece 1 of LIN-4219's approved plan: one owner for building a nested run's environment. **Lands first. No blockers.** Can run in parallel with piece 4.

## Slice of the approved plan

**File:** `test/child-env.js`, beside `test/isolate-run.js`, exporting `childEnv(mode, opts)`. It returns a fresh env object and never mutates `process.env`.

* `descendant`: keeps everything, including `NODE_OPTIONS` and `NODE_TEST_CONTEXT`, so the leak trap still covers it.
* `probe`: drops `NODE_TEST_CONTEXT` only and keeps `NODE_OPTIONS`.
* `run`: also drops `SD_TEST_RUN_ROOT`, `SD_TEST_ORIGINAL_TMPDIR`, `SD_TEST_VIOLATIONS_LOG` and `SD_STATE_DIR`. From `NODE_OPTIONS` it removes **only** the `--require` entries that name an `isolate-run.js` (from any checkout) and leaves every other option. The inner run adds its own preload.
* `opts.set` layers pins on top (`HARBOUR_DIR`, `TMPDIR`, …). `opts.drop` removes extra keys (for `state-dir.test.js`'s per-file overrides).
* The strip lists are **derived from** `isolate-run.js`**, not retyped**. `child-env.js` must **not** `require` `isolate-run.js`, because that file has side effects and a top-level `return`. A drift witness keeps the two files in step.

**Correction from plan review (note 5):** `isolate-run.js` also sets `TMPDIR` and `WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT`, and it rewrites `NODE_OPTIONS`. `run` mode keeps `TMPDIR` and `WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT` on purpose. Give `child-env.js` an explicit **kept-on-purpose list, with a reason for each entry**. The drift witness then asserts that dropped ∪ kept-on-purpose ∪ {`NODE_OPTIONS`, edited} covers every variable `isolate-run.js` added.

**Sites to move onto it.** There are seven: five from the plan plus two from review note 4. The census decides the final set, not this list.

1. `test/system/mutation/run-mutations.js` `killerEnvFor`: **delete it**. Today it keeps `NODE_OPTIONS`, so a killer in a copy preloads the live trap (`run-mutations.js:680-686`).
2. `test/state-dir.test.js` `envWithout`
3. `test/isolate-run.test.js` `runParent` / `runTestFileChild`
4. `test/leak-trap.test.js`: both env builders
5. `test/workspace-path-overrides.test.js:29` (`delete env.NODE_TEST_CONTEXT`, a probe)
6. `test/mutation-runner.test.js:113` (`NODE_OPTIONS: ''`, which strips preloads wholesale, the pattern the plan forbids). **Move it to** `childEnv('run')` **or** `'probe'`**. Do not allowlist it.** Line 218 of the same file builds the same env inside a template string, so make sure the census sees it or allowlist it with a written reason.

**Census, rule (b), lands here.** Add a census test in the `test/hook-driver-census.test.js` style, run in `npm test`. It fails on an env object that sets or deletes `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_TEST_CONTEXT`, `SD_TEST_RUN_ROOT`, `SD_TEST_ORIGINAL_TMPDIR`, `SD_TEST_VIOLATIONS_LOG` or `SD_STATE_DIR` outside `child-env.js`, `isolate-run.js` and `leak-trap.js`. As in the LIN-4183 census, the allowlist can only shrink, a stale entry fails, and every entry carries its reason. Pieces 3 and 4 add their own rules to this same census file. (Breakdown choice: each rule lands with the piece that empties its allowlist, so no rule lands red.) `{ ...process.env, … }` spreads that touch none of the six variables are plain descendants and are left alone.

## Testing strategy (witnesses, all in `npm test`)

1. **Fails today:** run a killer-style spawn through the mutation runner against a fixture copy, and assert that the killer's `NODE_OPTIONS` names no `isolate-run.js` outside the copy. Before the change, it names the live one.
2. **Drift test:** run `isolate-run.js` as a runner parent and as a test-file child (the helpers already in `isolate-run.test.js`). Diff the env before and after, and assert the cover rule from note 5 above. A new variable in `isolate-run.js` fails this test until `child-env.js` knows about it.
3. **Guard that must not go vacuous:** a `descendant` child with the trap preloaded still reports a leak it makes. This is the case wholesale stripping would break.

## Acceptance

* `childEnv` exists with the three modes. `killerEnvFor` is gone. All census-found env sites are moved or allowlisted with a reason.
* Witnesses 1–3 and census rule (b) pass in `npm test`. `npm run test:mutation` still runs green on its baseline.
* **Likeliest break (plan):** `run` strips too much (blinds the trap) or too little (leaves the live trap loaded). Witnesses 1 and 3 cover both directions.

---

**Parent:** LIN-4219 — *simple-dispatcher: the heavy test tier stands on one harness*. The parent's description holds the full scope, the "Done when" and "At merge" lists, the layout table and the **Implementation Plan**. Its comment trail holds the approving `### Plan Review Verdict` (comment `4ea51c1c-fa0a-44b9-9a63-c614f8fd7f56`). Read both before starting.

**Starting point:** the parent's approved plan is where this piece starts. Read it in full in LIN-4219's description, under "Implementation Plan". Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4219.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4219's approving plan-review (comment 4ea51c1c-fa0a-44b9-9a63-c614f8fd7f56, rev 1; the verdict names no revision number, and this is the only plan revision and the only verdict on the trail)
Grounding commit: simple-dispatcher `main` @ `502901c` (plan and review both grounded here; re-checked at breakdown on 2026-11-04, and nothing under `test/`, `docs/testing-and-ci.md`, `package.json` or `e2e-smoke.js` has changed)

**Constraints from the parent (all pieces):** nothing new at the repo root. `signal-guard.js` and `protected-paths.js` stay untouched. Each piece is its own PR, with its own run of `npm test`, plus `test:system` / `test:mutation` where the piece touches them. Out of scope, for the parent's close-out to list (not file): a scheduled/CI heavy-tier run (LIN-3160), pinned Harbour per dispatcher commit, splitting `run-mutations.js`, a test-infra module map, `e2e-smoke.js` joining the tier, the shared source sandbox.

## Implemented

Landed as [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/318](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/318>) (squash commit 52d2c3d, head 8133f3c). Implemented as the approved plan in LIN-4219, with these deviations: the strip list is derived from a new leaf `test/isolate-run-vars.js` that `isolate-run.js` writes through (not by parsing its source); the census found nine builders, not seven; `opts.from` is an extra seam. Nothing in this description was pruned: it holds only the problem, scope, testing strategy and acceptance, and the implementation plan lives in LIN-4219. The pre-close description is preserved in the task snapshots, and the full history is in the comment trail.

comments.body:
LIN-4220 (beat 5/5): PR is open for review.

- PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/318
- Head SHA: 8133f3c83fce9aa2fe01f0588f79561795c3a9ce (branch feat/lin-4220-child-env-nested-environment, base main)

Tests
- main (502901c): npm test 4023 total, 4018 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.
- This head: npm test 4123 total, 4118 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped, 0 todo (macOS, Node 25.9).
- npm run test:mutation: 67/67 killed, exit 0.

CI
- GitHub Actions "CI" / "unit tests" (ubuntu-latest, Node 22, npm ci + npm test) on 8133f3c: COMPLETED, SUCCESS. The repo's CI is the unit suite only; test:system, test:mutation and test:hooks are not in CI.

Known limitations (also in the PR description)
- `-r` (short form) in NODE_OPTIONS is not stripped by childEnv run mode; the spec names --require only.
- run mode keeps non-isolate NODE_OPTIONS entries where the old code wiped them; not observable under npm test.
- Census blind spots (listed in test/child-env-census.test.js header): computed keys, concatenated names, template substitutions, Reflect/defineProperty, non-JS env strings. The census scans test/** only.
- One characterization assertion was flipped (it pinned the killer NODE_OPTIONS defect).
- opts.from is a seam added beyond the spec.

Status left In Progress: review, merge and close-out are separate steps.

Autopilot (stepper) run summary, LIN-4220 implementation arc.

**Beats run** (one warm session, kind=implementation throughout):
1. Re-ground + characterize: branch, staleness check (none), real site list (nine builders vs the ticket's seven), 9 characterization cases, baseline 4023/4018 on main.
2. `test/child-env.js` + leaf `test/isolate-run-vars.js` (isolate-run.js: 9 write-side lines); 31 unit tests + 7-test runtime drift witness; failing-first and mutation evidence recorded.
3. All call sites migrated, `killerEnvFor` deleted, todo witness made real; mutation checks at killer / run / descendant sites; test:mutation 67/67.
4. Census (`test/child-env-census.test.js`) with 42-site / 27-entry reasoned allowlist, count ceilings, seeded-violation witnesses for all six names; isolate-run delta cases hardened (assertions unchanged).
5. Commit, push, PR, CI, Linear.

**Evidence (verified by me, not taken from the worker's report):** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/318 open against main, unmerged, head 8133f3c83fce9aa2fe01f0588f79561795c3a9ce; CI check "unit tests" COMPLETED/SUCCESS on that exact SHA; 13 files changed, all under test/ (no repo-root file; signal-guard.js and protected-paths.js untouched). Worker-reported: npm test 4123 total / 4118 pass / 0 fail / 5 skipped / 0 todo; test:mutation 67/67 killed.

**What holds:** the six census-tracked names can no longer be set or deleted outside child-env.js, isolate-run.js, leak-trap.js without an allowlisted, reasoned entry; the killer no longer inherits the live trap preload.

**What's left / not proven:** CI runs only the unit suite (not test:system, test:mutation, test:hooks), so those rest on the worker's local run. Known limitations are in the PR: `-r` short form not stripped; run mode keeps non-isolate NODE_OPTIONS; census blind spots; one flipped characterization assertion (it pinned the defect); `opts.from` seam beyond spec. Decisions I made: leaf-module derivation approved with a no-behaviour-change guard; census exempts `drop` inside `childEnv(` and not `set`.

Next: independent review (fresh session, dispatch 84b451ec-fb3d-4e1f-9d12-0f004db2a36f), then close-out. Merge and Done are not done.

## Review — LIN-4220

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/318 at head `8133f3c83fce9aa2fe01f0588f79561795c3a9ce` (base `main` @ `502901c`). Fresh session; every number below is from my own runs on macOS, Node 25.9.

CI: green. GitHub Actions "CI / unit tests" (ubuntu, Node 22, `npm test`) COMPLETED/SUCCESS on 8133f3c. CI runs only the unit suite, so I ran `test:mutation` and `test:system` myself (below).

### Scope vs plan
- 13 files, all under `test/`. No new repo-root files. `signal-guard.js` and `protected-paths.js` untouched. Staleness check: `main` has not moved since the ticket was created (still 502901c).
- `test/child-env.js` has the three modes as specified. It does not require `isolate-run.js`. Its strip list comes from a new leaf, `test/isolate-run-vars.js`, which `isolate-run.js` now also writes through (9 lines changed, behaviour unchanged; the drift witness pins this at runtime). Deriving the list from a shared leaf, instead of parsing the source, meets "derived, not retyped". `KEPT_ON_PURPOSE` gives a reason for `TMPDIR` and `WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT`.
- Sites: `killerEnvFor` is deleted. `envWithout` in state-dir and workspace-path-overrides, `runParent`, `runTestFileChild` and the twice-loaded case in isolate-run.test, both leak-trap builders plus the grandchild, and mutation-runner `:113` and the template at `:218` all go through `childEnv`. The census found nine builders where the ticket listed seven; the ticket says the census decides. None is left on ad hoc `NODE_OPTIONS` stripping.
- Old vs new semantics at each moved site: equivalent under `npm test`. The one intended difference is that `run` keeps non-isolate `NODE_OPTIONS` entries, which the old `runParent` and `mutation-runner` code wiped. The spec asks for exactly that.
- Open questions from the brief, settled:
  - **The non-isolate `NODE_OPTIONS` keep is witnessed.** The unit cases "keeps every other option byte-for-byte" and "removes entries from two checkouts…" pin it, and so does the killer-runtime case "CURRENT: an unrelated NODE_OPTIONS option is kept". Mutation M3 below turns all three red.
  - **The `-r` short form is outside the spec.** The spec names `--require`, and `isolate-run.js` writes only `--require "<path>"` (the drift witness pins that exact string). Accepted limitation, not a gap.
  - **`opts.from` is justified.** `runMutations` takes a caller `env`, so the killer site needs it.
  - **Census blind spots are stated in its header.** That is honest scope, not a defect.

### Regression check
`git log` on the touched files: LIN-4196 (copy-only edits), LIN-4181 (`WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT` pin), LIN-4077 (leak trap), LIN-3585 (trap preload for the mutation runner). All intact:
- `killerArgs` still preloads the copy's `isolate-run.js` and `state-cache-trap.js`.
- `runParent` still drops `WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT`.
- The trap still reaches descendants.
- `test:mutation` passes 67/67.
Nothing reverted is re-applied.

### Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards; `git status` clean)
- **M1:** killer site re-keeps the outer `NODE_OPTIONS` (old `killerEnvFor` behaviour). Characterization fails: "WITNESS: the killer NODE_OPTIONS names no isolate-run.js outside the copy" and "live checkout preload no longer reaches the killer" go red. Witness 1 holds.
- **M2:** `run` strips nothing from `NODE_OPTIONS`. Red in characterization, drift ("removes the isolate-run entry… and only that") and the unit table.
- **M3:** `run` wipes `NODE_OPTIONS` wholesale. Red: "CURRENT: an unrelated NODE_OPTIONS option is kept", "keeps every other option byte-for-byte", and the two-checkouts case.
- **M4:** `descendant` drops `NODE_OPTIONS`. Red: leak-trap "a descendant spawned with inherited NODE_OPTIONS is checked too", and drift "descendant keeps everything…". Witness 3 is not vacuous.
- **M5:** `isolate-run.js` sets a new `SD_TEST_NEWVAR`. Drift goes red ("sets exactly the keys the leaf declares" and "every key a preload adds is covered"). Witness 2 holds.
- **M6:** a seeded `{ ...process.env, NODE_OPTIONS: '' }` in state-dir.test.js. Census goes red.
- **M7:** an allowlisted leak-trap site is removed. Census goes red (stale entry, count and ceiling). The shrink-only rule holds.

### Class check
The class is "hand-built child env that sets or deletes a tracked name". `grep` across the repo, excluding `node_modules` and `docs`, finds none of the six names outside `test/` (including `e2e-smoke.js` and the shell scripts). Inside `test/`, the census is the enumeration, and every site it finds is either moved or allowlisted with a reason. No unhandled sibling inside the scope.

### Test runs (independent)
- **`npm test`:** PR head 4123 tests, 4118 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped. `main` 4023 tests, 4018 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped. Diffing failure and skip names between the two shows no change.
- **`npm run test:mutation`:**
  - PR head, run 1: the baseline failed on `test/system/wake-invariants.test.js` with ECONNREFUSED on its **fixed port 4141**, and no mutant ran.
  - PR head, run 2: 67/67 killed, exit 0.
  - `main` (with `HARBOUR_DIR` set to the sibling LinearViewer @ `eb44eff9`): 67/67, exit 0.
  - I read run 1 as a fixed-port flake, which is LIN-4222's class. This PR does not touch ports or the wake suite.
- **`npm run test:system`** (it preloads the edited `isolate-run.js`): PR head 119 tests, 117 pass, 2 fail. `main` has the same 117/2 with **identical failure names**: observation-feed "a completed standalone run appears as a terminal session…" and Tap 1 "generating a run summary drives Harbour's real OpenRouter client to the fake". These failures exist on main without this PR (Harbour @ `eb44eff9`) and are not a regression.

### Checklist
- Tests cover the new behaviour, and the mutations above prove they bite.
- No `process.env` mutation, per the unit "never mutates process.env" case.
- Bad mode or non-string pin throws a `TypeError`.
- Style matches the codebase.
- No security or performance concerns.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **`npm run test:mutation` stays green on its baseline** (acceptance). Inside: LIN-4220 acceptance, "test:mutation still runs green on its baseline". **Discharged**: re-run by review at 8133f3c, 67/67, exit 0.
- **`isolate-run.js` behaviour is unchanged under `test:system`** (it preloads the edited file). Inside: a claim this change depends on. **Discharged**: `test:system` failure names are identical on 8133f3c and 502901c.
- **The fixed-port flake: wake-invariants baseline ECONNREFUSED on port 4141, once in two PR-head runs.** Outside: port ownership is LIN-4222's bounded class, not this ticket's. Close-out should add the observation to LIN-4222, which already owns it, rather than file a new ticket.
- **Two `test:system` failures that also fail on main** (observation-feed Sessions view, Tap 1 OpenRouter fake). Outside: they exist on main and look Harbour-version related; pinning Harbour per dispatcher commit is out of scope per the parent. Close-out should check whether a ticket already exists and file only if none does.
- **The substitute runs have their usual limits.** Outside. They are one host (macOS, Node 25.9) with the sibling Harbour at `eb44eff9`, and they say nothing about commits after 8133f3c. Close-out re-checks CI on the exact merge commit.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

All inside items are already discharged by review's own runs. What remains for close-out is routing the outside observations (a note on LIN-4222, and a check for an existing ticket on the two pre-existing `test:system` failures) and re-checking CI on the merge commit. There are no code changes for close-out to make.

## Close-out — LIN-4220

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/318, squash-merged as `52d2c3d507ab933bf82128885249b6f24e890e0f`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 8133f3c83fce9aa2fe01f0588f79561795c3a9ce`. The review verdict was Approve, conditional on this close-out routing the outside items and re-checking CI. The merge was conflict-free, and `main` was still at 502901c when I merged.

**Changes I made after the approval:** none. Review asked for no code changes. Nothing stale was left behind (13 files, all under `test/`).

**CI:** GitHub Actions "CI / unit tests" was SUCCESS on the exact head 8133f3c before the merge. It is also SUCCESS on the merge commit 52d2c3d on `main` after the merge. CI runs only `npm test`.

**Deploy:** none. The change is test-harness only, with no product code and no deploy, so there were no post-deploy steps.

**Ledger**
- Inside, `test:mutation` green on its baseline: discharged by review. 67/67 killed, exit 0, on 8133f3c.
- Inside, `isolate-run.js` unchanged under `test:system`: discharged by review. The `test:system` failure names are identical on 8133f3c and 502901c.
- Outside, wake-invariants fixed-port 4141 ECONNREFUSED flake: I added the observation to LIN-4222, which already owns fixed ports, and filed no new ticket.
- Outside, two `test:system` failures that also fail on main: tickets already exist, so I filed nothing new. The observation-feed failure is LIN-4187. The Tap 1 OpenRouter failure is LIN-4188. I added a data-point comment to each and linked both as `related` to LIN-4220.
- Outside, substitute-run limits (one host, macOS/Node 25.9, Harbour eb44eff9): CI on the merge commit is re-checked and green, as above.

**Known limitations, accepted in review:** the `-r` short form in `NODE_OPTIONS` is not stripped; the census has stated blind spots; `opts.from` is a seam beyond the spec. These are documented in the PR and the census header.

**Description:** the pre-close description is snapshotted, and I confirmed it via `/snapshots`. I pruned nothing, because the description holds only problem, scope, testing strategy and acceptance, and the plan lives in LIN-4219. I appended an "Implemented" stub.

**Not run:** none.
